projection_to_consumer_inventory.finding: tap_types[] is the single most consistently and prominently rendered relationship-derived field across every consumer: Atlas's 'Tap types:' line on every one of 29 cards, Workflow's 'Relevant tap types' result section and T9 comparison row, Evidence's implicit tap-type cross-reference, and the CSV's 'tap_types' column. Every consumer faithfully displays whatever the projection says -- parity between consumers is certified. The risk is entirely upstream, at the relationship-resolution step in generate-tapping-projections.js, and would appear identically (and just as silently) in every product and the CSV simultaneously if it were ever wrong.

silent_drop_audit.conclusion: No newly-discovered field is silently dropped between layers. The material finding this session is not a drop but an unguarded relationship-DERIVATION (tap_types[]).

primary_finding.source: data/relationships/relationships.seed.json's RELATES_TO edges where source == profile.operation (e.g. 'cut_tapping'), resolved via resolveEntityContext() in scripts/utilities/relationship-resolver.js, filtered to entity_type === 'tap_type'
primary_finding.current_live_data: All 29 profiles use operation='cut_tapping'. cut_tapping's OWN entity.related_entities array is EMPTY -- the entire relationship comes from 5 separate RELATES_TO records in relationships.seed.json: cut_tapping->taper_tap, cut_tapping->plug_tap, cut_tapping->bottoming_tap, cut_tapping->spiral_point_tap, cut_tapping->spiral_flute_tap. All 29 profiles therefore resolve to the identical 5-element set. hand_tap and forming_tap are correctly excluded (not connected to cut_tapping).
primary_finding.evidence: validate-tapping-projections.js check 2 only confirms `entityIds.has(tapTypeId)` for each element already present in row.tap_types -- pure existence. No check independently re-derives the expected set from relationships.seed.json + profile.operation and compares it to the projection's actual tap_types[] array.
primary_finding.mutation_test_feasibility: high -- temporarily remove or add one RELATES_TO record touching cut_tapping in relationships.seed.json, leave the projection unregenerated, confirm a new check would fail; identical proven technique to T13-T16.

relationship_resolution_audit.existence_vs_membership_gap_confirmed: Exactly the pattern the phase brief called out: 'relationship resolution that proves existence but not correct relationship membership.' Every element of tap_types[] independently resolves to a real tap_type entity (existence, checked), but nothing confirms the SET as a whole is what the relationship graph currently establishes for that profile's operation (membership/correctness, unchecked).

aggregation_count_audit.finding: All rendered, user-facing counts (9/20, 0/29, 1/15) are dynamically re-derived from the projection at validation time in every consumer's own validator, never hardcoded -- reconfirmed unchanged. profileProjection.data_quality_summary is itself an aggregate but is never consumed (Section on candidates, not selected).

selected_t17_target.title: Tap-Type Relationship-Membership Verification
selected_t17_target.objective: Add a validator check that independently re-derives the expected tap_types[] set for every profile directly from relationships.seed.json's RELATES_TO edges for that profile's operation entity, and compares it to the projection's actual tap_types[] array.
selected_t17_target.root_risk: buildProfileRows() resolves tap_types[] via resolveEntityContext(profile.operation), which walks the relationship graph; the existing validator only confirms each resulting ID is a real entity, never that the SET is what the current relationship graph actually establishes. A future edit to relationships.seed.json (an added or removed RELATES_TO edge) combined with a stale, unregenerated projection would show the wrong 'relevant tap types' on every affected product, and every existing validator would still pass.
selected_t17_target.source_of_truth: data/relationships/relationships.seed.json's RELATES_TO records where source equals the profile's operation entity id, plus data/entities/entities.seed.json for entity_type filtering (both already loaded by validate-tapping-projections.js via knowledge.relationships and knowledge.entities)
selected_t17_target.affected_consumers: data/projections/tapping/tapping-profiles.json's tap_types[] directly; indirectly every product's 'Relevant/relevant tap types' section and the CSV's tap_types column
selected_t17_target.exact_gap: No check independently re-derives the expected tap_types set from the relationship graph and compares it to the projection.
selected_t17_target.not_already_covered_by: T13 (tap_drill.status), T14 (tap_drill.convention/provenance narrative), T15 (application_notes.source), T16 (standards[] denormalization) -- four distinct, already-named field families; this is relationship-derived membership, untouched by any of them.

forbidden_files: data/relationships/relationships.seed.json (except as a temporary, restored mutation fixture)
implementation_contract.validator_behavior_required: For each profile row, need to determine the operation entity id (this requires either reading it from the source dataset record via a new tapping_profile_id-keyed lookup, similar to check 10/11's sourceRecordById pattern, since profile.operation is not itself carried into the projection row). For that operation id, collect all RELATES_TO relationship records where source equals the operation id and target is a tap_type entity; sort; compare to row.tap_types (sorted). Fail on any set difference.
implementation_contract.pass_criteria: 0 errors on real data (already confirmed the current set is correct by direct inspection); correct failure on a reproduced relationship-graph mutation; all other validators unaffected; every checksum outside the validator itself unchanged

mutation_test_contract.method: Temporarily remove one RELATES_TO record (e.g. rel_cut_tapping_relates_taper_tap) from data/relationships/relationships.seed.json, backed up first, WITHOUT regenerating the projection.
mutation_test_contract.expected_result: FAIL, identifying the affected profiles (all 29, since all share operation='cut_tapping') and the specific missing/extra tap_type
mutation_test_contract.restoration: restore from backup, confirm byte-identical checksum, confirm validator returns to PASS

selected_t17_target.determinism_requirement: validator run 3x on restored real data, byte-identical report

implementation.check_added: Tap-Type Relationship Membership Matches Authoritative RELATES_TO Graph
implementation.mechanism: For each of the 29 profiles: resolves operation from the source dataset record via sourceRecordById; collects every RELATES_TO relationship whose source is that operation and whose target is a tap_type entity (via tapTypeEntitiesById); sorts the expected id set; sorts the projection's actual tap_types[]; computes the full missing/unexpected symmetric difference (not merely length or per-id existence); fails on any mismatch, naming the profile, designation, operation, and both difference lists.

mutation_failure.method: Temporarily edited the real data/relationships/relationships.seed.json (backed up first), removing the rel_cut_tapping_relates_taper_tap record entirely (41 records -> 40), WITHOUT regenerating either projection.
mutation_failure.sample_error_message: tap_m10x1_25_cut (designation M10x1.25, operation 'cut_tapping'): tap_types[] membership mismatch -- missing: [none], unexpected: [taper_tap]
mutation_failure.note: taper_tap correctly reported as 'unexpected' rather than 'missing' -- the removed edge means the graph no longer establishes it, but the stale, unregenerated projection still carries it. All 29 errors independently confirmed to name taper_tap as the sole discrepancy.
